# What policies can RL learn that IL cannot?

This might sounds like a very naive question.


# Policy optimisation

From an information-theoretic viewpoint, policy learning is all about doing optimisation to arrive at a _useful_ policy. Usefulness here is understood as having utility

Conceptually we have two tools available to us,
- The forward Kullback-Liebler (KL) divergence
- The reverse KL divergence.

The distinction between forward- and reverse-KL is terminology that resides only the context of optimisation. One should think of $\pi(\cdot | x)$ as the policy under optimisation


## Forward KL-divergence

$$
\min_\pi D_\text{KL}(\pi^\ast||\pi) = \max_\pi \left \{ \mathbb{E}_{\pi^\ast} \left [ \log \pi(y|x) \right ] + H[\pi^\ast(y|x)] \right \} = \max_\pi \mathbb{E}_{\pi^\ast} \left [ \log \pi(y|x) \right ]
$$

## Reverse KL-divergence

$$
\min_\pi D_\text{KL}(\pi||\pi^\ast) = \max_\pi \left \{\mathbb{E}_\pi \left [ \log \pi^\ast(y|x) \right ] + H[\pi(y|x)] \right \}
$$

---

## Imitation learning

In imitation learning, the learner is provided with trajectories from what is considered to be a expert policy $\pi^\ast$ and is trained to imitate the actions of the expert. This falls cleanly into the __forward KL__ formulation.

## Reinforcement learning

While we in the forward objective can compute the expectation using samples from $\pi^\ast$, in the reverse objective we do not have access to a closed-form expression of the probability density $\pi^\ast$. Typically in RL, we consider this density to be induced by a reward function $R(x, y) \in \mathbb{R}$. We can interpret $R$ as the joint energy between a state and action. Ideally we would want (state, action)-pairs with high reward to be more probable, this is achieved through the Boltzmann distribution

$$
p_R(y|x) = \frac{1}{Z(x)} \exp \left ( \frac{1}{\beta} R(x,y) \right)
$$

Which then ends up giving us the objective

$$
\min_\pi D_\text{KL}(\pi||\pi^\ast) = \max_\pi \left \{ \frac{1}{\beta} \mathbb{E}_\pi \left [R(x, y) \right ] + H[\pi(y|x)] - \log Z(x) \right \} =  \max_\pi \left \{ \mathbb{E}_\pi \left [R(x, y) \right ]  + \beta H[\pi(y|x)] \right \}
$$

In recent years it has been popular to optimise the regularised reward objective,

$$
\bar{R}(x, y) = R(x,y) - \beta \log \pi_\text{ref}(y|x)
$$

which then leads to

$$
\min_\pi D_\text{KL}(\pi||\pi^\ast) =  \max_\pi \left \{ \mathbb{E}_\pi \left [R(x, y) \right ]  + \beta D_\text{KL}(\pi||\pi_\text{ref}) \right \}
$$

## A new objective

$$
\mathcal{J} =  \mathbb{E}_\pi \left [R(x, y) \right ]  + \beta H(\pi, \pi^\ast) + (1 - \beta) H(\pi)
$$
